svg.title: LZ77 over "abracadabra abracadabra": each match found on the hash chain of its first three bytes

g.title: At 0: "abr" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'a' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first
empty: nothing has been seen yet

g.title: At 1: "bra" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'b' goes out as a literal. The places before it are in the table now, each at the head of the chain of its three bytes.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 2: "rac" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'r' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 3: "aca" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'a' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 4: "cad" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'c' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 5: "ada" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'a' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 6: "dab" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'd' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 7: the chain of "abr" holds 0; tried nearest first, place 0 gives 4 bytes. The longest wins: a match, 7 back, 4 bytes, "abra".
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 11: " ab" has not been seen before (its chain is empty), so 'space' goes out as a literal.
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first

g.title: At 12: the chain of "abr" holds 7, 0; tried nearest first, place 7 gives 4 bytes, place 0 gives 11 bytes. The longest wins: a match, 12 back, 11 bytes, "abracadabra".
g.text: the hash table: for each hash, a chain of the places that had it, newest first
